newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq opposes Turkish military measures in north.
newsitem.headline: Iraq opposes Turkish military measures in north.

text.p: Iraq has summoned a senior Turkish diplomat in Baghdad to complain about Ankara's military build-up along the border with Kurdish-held northern Iraq.

Baghdad newspapers said on Friday Foreign Minister Mohammed Saeed al-Sahaf summoned Turkish acting charge d'affaires at midnight on Thursday over "Turkey's attitude vis-a-vis recent developments in northern Iraq."

"The foreign minister told the acting Turkish charge d'affaires on Thursday midnight...to convey formally to the Turkish government a number of points regarding Turkey's declared stand over latest developments in northern Iraq.

"The foreign minister informed the acting Turkish charge d'affaires of Iraq's rejection of Turkish military measures on Iraqi borders because they constituted a totally unjustified conduct and a violation of Iraq's sovereignty and territorial integrity," the papers said.
Turkey is planning to create a security zone in northern Iraq up to 10 km (six miles) deep and Washington said on Wednesday it would not object if Ankara went ahead with the scheme.
There was heavy military activity on the Turkish side of the frontier with Iraq on Thursday, but Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller said a thrust across the border was not imminent.

The two countries usually coordinate on how to curb their rebelloius Kurds. Baghdad diplomats said Iraq had informed Turkey of its military assault on the Kurdish city of Arbil, captured last weekend.

Apart from the summoning of the Turkish envoy there was no other word in the state-run newspapers on Friday of Ankara's military build-up along the Iraqi border and its intention of securing a strip of territory inside Iraq to check attacks by its own rebel Kurds.
